questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following polymers in an increasing order of intermolecular forces; fibre, plastic, elastomer.
questions.solution:
Elastomers or rubbers have the weakest intermolecular forces of attraction followed by plastics while fibres have the strongest forces of attraction. Thus, the increasing intermolecular forces of attraction follows the order

elastomer < plastic < fibre.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Polyethylene is obtained from calcium carbide.

$Ca{C}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O \to Ca{\left(OH\right)}_{2} + {C}_{2}{H}_{2}$

${C}_{2}{H}_{2} + {H}_{2} \to {C}_{2}{H}_{4}$

$n{C}_{2}{H}_{4} \to \left(- C{H}_{2} - C{H}_{2} -\right)n$

Therefore, the amount of polyethylene (in kg) obtained for 64 kg $Ca{C}_{2}$ is
questions.solution:
Moles of $Ca{C}_{2} = \dfrac{64 \times 1{0}^{3}}{64} ≅ 1 \times 1{0}^{3}$

So from the balanced chemical equation, moles of ${C}_{2}{H}_{2} =$ moles of ${C}_{2}{H}_{4}$

$=$ moles of $Ca{C}_{2} = 1 \times 1{0}^{3}$

So moles of polythene $= \dfrac{1}{n} \times 1 \times 1{0}^{3}$

So weight of polythene $= \dfrac{1}{n} \times 1 \times 1 \times 28n$ kg

= 28 kg
